roles.name: Trustee for CPP / OAS benefits of an incapable beneficiary
localNames: person or agency to whom the benefit is paid on behalf of a beneficiary
roles.summary: If the Minister is satisfied that a beneficiary is incapable of managing their own affairs, CPP or OAS benefits can be paid to a person or agency on the beneficiary's behalf. That is a legally authorized manager (such as a provincial attorney or guardian) or, failing one, a person or agency the Minister approves who signs an agreement to administer the benefits. The trustee must account and must return payments issued after the month of death.

assigned.event: Minister is satisfied, on medical or other evidence (in practice a Certificate of Incapability, ISP-3505), that the beneficiary cannot manage their own affairs, and directs payment to a legally authorized person or agency or, if none, to a Minister-approved person or agency

starts.event: Once the person or agency has signed the agreement to administer the benefits (ISP-3506 private / ISP-3507 agency). Under the CPP Regulations, no benefit may be paid to them until they do.

ends.event: Beneficiary dies: CPP retirement and OAS pensions stop with the payment for the month of death, and the trustee must return uncashed payments and any issued after that month
Beneficiary stops being incapable of managing their own affairs: the trustee must notify ESDC, and the legal basis for a direction under s 55 / s 24 falls away
ends.note: Neither regulation has an express revocation clause. The end on regaining capacity is inferred from the incapacity precondition and from the notice duty in the ISP-3506 undertaking.

ends.event: The trusteeship ends for another reason, e.g. the trustee withdraws or the Minister redirects payment (the trustee must notify ESDC)

notes.text: A provincially authorized manager (e.g. an attorney under a continuing/enduring POA or a guardian of property) is preferred: the Minister pays that person or agency, and appoints a Minister-approved trustee only where no one is so authorized.
Separate rules let another person or agency apply, or seek reconsideration or appeal, on behalf of an incapable person (CPP Regs ss 44, 74; OAS Regs s 4).
The trustee must account in the form and at the times the Minister requires. The ISP-3506 undertaking also requires yearly records.
CPP section numbers: payment to another person is CPP Regulations s 55, not s 57. OAS: s 24, not s 34.

Minister satisfied of incapability and has identified a payee; agreement not yet signed
Benefits paid to the trustee, who administers them for the beneficiary
Payment held pending agreement, accounting request or change of trustee (administrative)
Beneficiary died, regained capacity, or trusteeship ended

transitions.event: Minister directs payment to a person or agency on the incapable beneficiary's behalf
conditions: Evidence satisfactory to the Minister of incapacity to manage own affairs

transitions.event: Payee signs the agreement to administer and spend the benefit for the beneficiary
Payment withheld pending accounting or change of trustee
Beneficiary dies; pension stops after the month of death, and later payments must be returned
Beneficiary ceases to be incapable of managing own affairs (trustee must notify ESDC)

roles.name: Legal representative of a deceased taxpayer (CRA)
roles.summary: The Income Tax Act defines a deceased taxpayer's legal representative as the executor, administrator, liquidator, heir or similar fiduciary dealing with the estate. That person files the final return (due by the later of the normal due date and six months after death, for deaths after October). They must get a clearance certificate before distributing property, or they are personally liable for unpaid tax.

assigned.event: Appointment under provincial law (executor named in a will, court-appointed administrator/estate trustee, Quebec liquidator). The CRA registers the person on receiving the death certificate and the will, grant or letters, or Form RC552 if there is no will.

starts.event: On death. The statutory filing duty falls on the legal representatives. CRA access to the deceased's tax records follows once the documents are processed.

ends.event: Tax liabilities settled and a clearance certificate obtained before final distribution. Distributing without one makes the representative personally liable up to the value distributed.
The provincial fiduciary office ends (removal, renunciation, replacement). CRA representation follows the underlying appointment.

notes.text: The definition is functional ('or any other like person ... dealing in a representative or fiduciary capacity'), so it covers whoever holds the provincial estate office, not a CRA appointment.

Authorized representatives the taxpayer appointed during life (e.g. via Represent a Client / AUT-01) keep access after the CRA is notified of death unless they were the legal representative. They stay until a legal representative asks for their removal.

states.label: No person recognised as legal representative
Named or appointed under provincial law; CRA not yet notified or documents pending
Recognised by CRA; files returns, deals with balances, requests clearance certificate
Clearance obtained and estate distributed, or fiduciary office ended

transitions.event: Taxpayer dies; executor/administrator/liquidator holds the office under provincial law
CRA receives death certificate plus will/grant/letters, or RC552
Clearance certificate obtained and property distributed

roles.name: Legal representative of a living taxpayer who cannot act (CRA)
roles.summary: If an individual cannot file their own return, the Income Tax Act lets their guardian, committee or other legal representative file it. The CRA recognises as legal representative a person appointed by a legal document: a court-appointed guardian, trustee or committee, a person named in a power of attorney, or a representative under a BC-style representation agreement. The authority comes from, and ends with, that provincial instrument.

assigned.event: Provincial instrument or order: power of attorney, representation agreement, or court appointment as guardian/trustee/committee

starts.event: When the underlying instrument is in effect and the CRA has received a copy (Represent a Client RepID linked to the taxpayer). The statutory filing role applies when the person cannot file for any reason.

ends.event: Taxpayer dies: the living-person authority ends under provincial law and the estate's legal representative takes over. CRA says only a legal representative's access ends on notice of death.
Underlying POA/guardianship is revoked or terminated under provincial law

notes.text: This is different from an 'authorized representative' the taxpayer appoints (Represent a Client / AUT-01). That access lasts until cancelled or until an optional expiry date, and CRA says it does not expire when the CRA is notified of death.

states.label: No legal document appointing a representative
POA/order exists; not yet filed with CRA or not yet in effect
CRA recognises the legal representative for the taxpayer's accounts
Taxpayer died or the instrument ended

transitions.event: POA executed, representation agreement made, or guardian/committee appointed
Copy of legal document submitted and RepID linked
Taxpayer dies; access as legal representative ends on CRA notification
Instrument revoked or guardianship terminated under provincial law

roles.name: Administrator of a Pension Act award for an incapable recipient (Veterans Affairs Canada)
localNames: person or agency selected by the Minister
roles.summary: Under the Pension Act, if a person entitled to an award appears to the Minister to be incapable of managing their own affairs, the Minister may direct that the award be administered for them by the Department or by a person or agency the Minister selects. No equivalent provision was found in the Veterans Well-being Act or its Regulations.

assigned.event: Minister directs administration of the award because it appears the recipient cannot manage their own affairs because of infirmity, illness or other cause

ends.event: Recipient dies: the award stops, and amounts paid after the last day of the month of death can be recovered from survivor awards
ends.note: Section 83(5) implies awards stop after the month of death. No express 'administration ends on death' text was found.

ends.event: The Minister revokes or changes the direction (e.g. the recipient regains capacity)

notes.text: The Veterans Well-being Act (SC 2005, c 21) and the Veterans Well-being Regulations (SOR/2006-50) were searched. Neither has a comparable provision on administration for incapable recipients. The distinct statutory regime is only the Pension Act s 41.

states.label: Award administered by the Department or a selected person/agency

transitions.event: Minister directs administration of the award
conditions: Appears to the Minister that the person is incapable of managing their own affairs (or is not maintaining a dependant for whom additional pension is paid)

roles.name: Estate administrator exercising Privacy Act rights for a deceased person (federal institutions)
localNames: person authorized ... to administer the estate of that person
roles.summary: For personal information held by federal government institutions (including health and benefits records), the Privacy Regulations let a person authorized under federal or provincial law to administer a deceased person's estate exercise that person's Privacy Act rights, only for administering the estate. Information about someone dead more than 20 years is not 'personal information' for the use, disclosure and ATIA s 19 rules.

assigned.event: Appointment as estate administrator under provincial law (executor, estate trustee, liquidator, administrator)

starts.event: On authority to administer the estate

ends.event: Estate administration ends (rights exist 'only for the purpose of such administration')
More than 20 years after death: the information is excluded from 'personal information' for Privacy Act ss 7, 8 and 26 and ATIA s 19

notes.text: Section 10(a) of the Privacy Regulations likewise lets a person authorized to administer the affairs or estate of an incompetent person exercise that person's rights while they are alive.

states.label: May exercise Privacy Act rights for estate administration
Administration complete or information older than 20 years post-death

transitions.event: Person becomes authorized to administer the estate

deceasedPersonalDataProtected.note: The federal law is split. (1) Public sector, Privacy Act: information about a person dead more than 20 years is excluded from 'personal information' for use and disclosure (ss 7, 8), s 26 and ATIA s 19. Within 20 years it stays protected, and an estate administrator may exercise the deceased's rights only for administration (Privacy Regs s 10(b)). (2) Private sector, PIPEDA: 'personal information' is information about an identifiable individual with no living-person limit. 'Personal health information' expressly covers an individual 'whether living or deceased'. Organizations may disclose without consent 20 years after death or 100 years after the record was created (s 7(3)(h)). OPC guidance limits a deceased's account information to the person authorized to administer the estate, and a beneficiary may access only information about themselves. PIPEDA does not apply where a substantially similar provincial law applies (e.g. Quebec, BC, Alberta private sector), and provincial health-information statutes govern many health records. Bill C-36 (introduced 15 June 2026, at second reading) would replace PIPEDA Part 1 with the Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act.
unverified_components: The OPC statement that PIPEDA covers deceased individuals was not found verbatim on an OPC page. This conclusion rests on the statute text (s 2(1), s 7(3)(h)) and the OPC guidance on deceased account holders.

digitalAssetsFiduciaryStatute.note: Not set nationally: fiduciary access to digital assets is provincial or territorial. See modelActs (ULCC Uniform Access to Digital Assets by Fiduciaries Act, 2016) for enacting jurisdictions.

modelActs.name: Uniform Access to Digital Assets by Fiduciaries Act
modelActs.summary: Covers four fiduciaries: a personal representative, a guardian, an attorney under a POA, and a trustee. Confirms that their usual powers extend to digital assets, subject to the account holder's instructions. A personal representative gets access to all digital assets unless the will or another document says otherwise.

modelActs.name: Uniform Enduring Powers of Attorney Act
modelActs.summary: Model EPOA takes effect on the latest of signing, a stated date or a stated triggering event (s 11(1)). If it springs on incapacity, a qualified health care provider may confirm incapacity (s 11(2)). Authority ends on a specified date, written revocation, the grantor's death, the attorney's death, incapacity or resignation, appointment of a guardianship decision-maker, and spousal separation (s 17). The 2021 amendments added electronic EPOAs. The year is 2015 (amended 2021), not 2008.
modelActs.enactmentsNote: No provincial or territorial enactment of the 2015 Uniform EPOA Act was verified. Several provinces have EPOA statutes that share features, but none was confirmed as an implementation of this model act.

provincialNotes.text: Nova Scotia's Human Organ and Tissue Donation Act, SNS 2019, c 6, deems an individual who has not recorded a consent or refusal to consent to donation (s 11). Exceptions cover lack of capacity, non-residents and minors (ss 12–14). Proclaimed June 30, 2020; in force January 18, 2021 (per the official consolidation, current to June 18, 2026, as amended by 2025, c 2, s 6).
